findings.title: Unsafe destructuring can crash booking creation when no destination calendar exists
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` accesses `.integration` without an optional chain. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`/`undefined`/`[]` (e.g. the booking organizer has no destination calendar configured) and the chosen location is Google Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, and the comparison throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, crashing `EventManager.create()`. Previously this used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== ...`), which safely evaluated to true. This regression can break every new booking that selects Google Meet without a connected Google Calendar.

findings.title: Broken fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent/deleteEvent always resolves to undefined
findings.body: In both `updateEvent` (line 256) and `deleteEvent` (line 317) the fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` — but this code only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the ternary's else branch), so the `.find` predicate compares `cal.externalId` against the same falsy value that triggered the fallback. This will essentially never match a real destination calendar entry, so `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` resolves to `undefined` whenever no `externalCalendarId` is supplied (e.g. for older booking references without a stored externalCalendarId). Previously the fallback correctly used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. This breaks updating/deleting Google Calendar events for any booking reference lacking an externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Only Google Calendar filters destinationCalendar by credentialId; other calendar apps always use the first host's calendar
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` iterates `event.destinationCalendar` (which now contains one entry per host for collective events) and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each host's credential, but the full, unfiltered `event` object (with the complete destinationCalendar array for all hosts) is passed to every calendar provider's `createEvent`. Only `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts) actually uses the `credentialId` argument to pick the matching destination calendar entry. Office365 (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 72-77), Lark (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 125-129), and the CalDAV-based `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (lines 156-166) all just destructure `event.destinationCalendar[0]` as the 'main host' regardless of which host's credential is currently creating the event. As a result, for collective events where the second (or later) host uses Office365/Lark/CalDAV, the event will be created against the first host's calendar externalId using the second host's credentials — the wrong calendar, or an inaccessible one — defeating the PR's stated purpose for every non-Google calendar integration.

findings.title: Inverted condition for assigning organization slug vs requiring billing
findings.body: The condition for setting the `slug` field was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting the original intent. Previously the subdomain `slug` was only assigned directly when team billing was NOT required (so no payment gate was needed); when billing was enabled, only `metadata.requestedSlug` was set pending payment. With this change, `slug` is now set immediately when billing IS enabled (potentially letting an org claim a subdomain before completing required payment) and is never set when billing is disabled (orgs created in that mode end up with no slug at all). This change is unrelated to the PR's stated destinationCalendar fix and appears to be an accidental regression carried in from elsewhere.

findings.title: Recurring-event calendar deletion logic runs once per calendar reference, duplicating deletes
findings.body: The outer loop over `bookingCalendarReference` was changed from a single `.find()` result to `.filter()` plus a `for` loop to support multiple hosts/credentials. However, the nested recurring-event branch (lines 444-468) that deletes every remaining recurring booking instance from `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and `updatedBookings` is executed on every iteration of the outer loop. For a collective booking with N calendar references (N hosts with credentialId set), this recurring-deletion pass — which already iterates all organizer calendar credentials and all updatedBookings internally — now runs N times, issuing duplicate `deleteEvent` calls for the same bookings/credentials. This is wasteful, risks extra/duplicate calendar API calls, and can surface spurious errors.

findings.title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: After building `evt`, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` guarded only for COLLECTIVE events. `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. In that case the optional chaining makes `push` a no-op, so the destination calendars collected for the other (non-organizer) hosts in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded and those hosts never receive calendar invites for a collective event. This is exactly the multi-host scenario the PR claims to fix, so the fix fails for organizers without a configured destination calendar.

findings.title: organization.slug dropped from the dynamic-booking user select without apparent replacement
findings.body: In the rewritten `loadUsers` function, the `prisma.user.findMany` select for the dynamic (no-eventTypeId) booking path used to include `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`, but this field was removed in the rewrite (only `...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true` remain). If any downstream logic in the dynamic booking flow (e.g. building org-aware links or multi-tenant routing) relies on `user.organization.slug`, it will now silently be `undefined`. This field removal is unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR (destinationCalendar array support) and looks like an unintentional regression.

findings.title: No test coverage added for the actual multi-host destinationCalendar behavior
findings.body: The PR converts `destinationCalendar` to an array across ~20 files and changes behavior for collective events with multiple hosts, but the only test changes are updates to expected JSON shape (`destinationCalendar: null` -> `destinationCalendar: []`) in existing single-host webhook e2e tests. The PR description itself states 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works.' There is no test verifying that a collective event with two hosts using different calendar credentials actually results in calendar invites being created in each host's correct calendar — the exact scenario this PR is meant to fix, and the area where several of the above bugs (e.g. non-Google calendar providers always using host #1's calendar) would have been caught.

findings.title: Inconsistent empty-value representation for destinationCalendar across handlers
findings.body: Different handlers normalize a missing destination calendar differently now that the field is an array: `confirm.handler.ts` (line 179), `webhook.ts`, `paypal-webhook.ts`, and `deleteCredential.handler.ts` fall back to `[]`, while `handleNewBooking.ts` falls back to `null`. Consumers of the webhook payload (and any other code reading `evt.destinationCalendar`) now observe different representations (`null` vs `[]`) for the logically identical 'no destination calendar' state depending on which code path produced the event, which is an inconsistent contract that can break strict-equality checks or type assumptions downstream.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch call can target an undefined calendarId
findings.body: In `createEvent`, the initial `calendar.events.insert` call uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, defaulting to `"primary"` when no destination calendar matches the current `credentialId`. However, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch(...)` call made when a hangout link is present (line 168) uses the raw `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without the same `|| "primary"` fallback. If no destination calendar entry matches the credential (so `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`), the event is inserted into `"primary"` but the subsequent patch to add the hangout link to the description targets an undefined calendar id, which will likely fail silently or error out, leaving the event without the hangout link update.
